steps.title: Congruent means identical
steps.body: Two shapes are **congruent** if one is an exact copy of the other: every side and every angle matches. It may be rotated or flipped over. The two triangles below are congruent even though one is upside down.

visuals.alt: Two congruent triangles with sides 7, 5, 6, one rotated and flipped, matching sides marked with the same ticks

check.prompt: A triangle is reflected in a mirror line. Is the image congruent to the original?
check.solution: Reflection changes position and orientation, not size or shape.
options: Only if it is not rotated

steps.title: SSS: three sides
steps.body: If the three sides of one triangle equal the three sides of another, the triangles are congruent. You met the reason in constructions: three sides fix the triangle completely.

visuals.alt: Two triangles with all three pairs of sides marked equal

visuals.problem: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = 6$ cm, $BC = 8$ cm, $AC = 10$ cm. Triangle $PQR$ has $PQ = 6$ cm, $QR = 8$ cm, $PR = 10$ cm. Prove that the triangles are congruent.

steps.text: $AB = PQ = 6$ cm (given)
$BC = QR = 8$ cm (given)
$AC = PR = 10$ cm (given)
So triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $PQR$ by SSS. Write all three matching pairs, then name the condition.

check.prompt: Triangle 1 has sides 5, 6, 7. Triangle 2 has sides 7, 5, 6. Are they congruent?
check.solution: Same three lengths: the order they are listed in does not matter.
options: No, the sides are in a different order
Only if the angles are also given

steps.title: SAS: two sides and the included angle
steps.body: Two sides and the angle **between** them. The angle must be the included one: it is the angle where the two equal sides meet.

visuals.alt: Two triangles with two pairs of equal sides and the angle between them marked equal

visuals.problem: In triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$, $AB = DE = 5$ cm, $BC = EF = 7$ cm and angle $ABC$ = angle $DEF$ = $50°$. Prove that the triangles are congruent.

steps.text: $AB = DE = 5$ cm (given)
Angle $ABC$ = angle $DEF$ = $50°$ (given). This is the angle between the two known sides in both triangles, so it is the included angle.
$BC = EF = 7$ cm (given)
So triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $DEF$ by SAS. If the equal angle were at $A$ or $C$ instead, it would not be included and SAS could not be used.

check.prompt: $AB = DE$, $AC = DF$ and angle $A$ = angle $D$. Which condition applies?
check.solution: Angle $A$ is between $AB$ and $AC$, and angle $D$ is between $DE$ and $DF$: SAS.

steps.title: ASA: two angles and a side
steps.body: Two angles and the side between them. If the equal side is **not** between the equal angles, find the third angle with the angle sum: two matching angles force the third to match, so the side is now between two known angles. Some books call this AAS; on the exam, quoting ASA after finding the third angle is fine.

visuals.alt: Two triangles with two pairs of equal angles and the side between them marked equal

visuals.problem: Triangle $ABC$ has angle $A = 40°$, angle $B = 60°$ and $AB = 7$ cm. Triangle $XYZ$ has angle $X = 40°$, angle $Z = 80°$ and $XY = 7$ cm. Prove that the triangles are congruent.

steps.text: Angle sum in $XYZ$: angle $Y = 180° - 40° - 80° = 60°$
Angle $A$ = angle $X$ = $40°$ and angle $B$ = angle $Y$ = $60°$
$AB = XY = 7$ cm, and in both triangles this side is between the two equal angles
So triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $XYZ$ by ASA

check.prompt: Triangle 1 has angles $40°$ and $75°$. Triangle 2 has angles $40°$ and $65°$. What is the third angle of triangle 2?
check.solution: $180 - 40 - 65 = 75°$, so the triangles have the same three angles.

steps.title: RHS: right angle, hypotenuse, side
steps.body: For right-angled triangles only: equal hypotenuses and one other pair of equal sides. It works because Pythagoras then fixes the third side, turning it into SSS.

visuals.alt: Two right-angled triangles with the hypotenuse 5 and the 3 cm side both ticked as equal in each

visuals.problem: Triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are right-angled at $B$ and $E$. $AC = DF = 13$ cm and $BC = EF = 5$ cm. Prove that the triangles are congruent.

steps.text: Angle $ABC$ = angle $DEF$ = $90°$ (given)
$AC = DF = 13$ cm: the hypotenuses are equal
$BC = EF = 5$ cm: one other pair of sides is equal
So triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $DEF$ by RHS. Pythagoras confirms $AB = DE = 12$ cm, so SSS would also have worked.

check.prompt: Two right-angled triangles have hypotenuse 25 cm and one side 7 cm. What is the third side of each?
check.solution: $25^2 - 7^2 = 625 - 49 = 576$, so 24 cm in both. RHS is SSS in disguise.

steps.title: Why SSA is not on the list
steps.body: Two sides and an angle that is not between them can be arranged into two different triangles. This is the ambiguous case from constructions, and it is why SSA is not a condition for congruence: two triangles can share all three of those measurements and still not be the same shape.

visuals.alt: Two different triangles that both have sides 7 and 5 and a 40 degree angle not between them

visuals.problem: Two triangles from the same SSA

steps.text: Draw $AB = 7$ cm and an angle of $40°$ at $A$
Set compasses to $5$ cm at $B$ and swing an arc across the line from $A$
The arc crosses that line twice, so there are two positions for $C$
The two triangles have different third sides and different angles at $C$: not congruent. SSA proves nothing

steps.title: Your turn: use congruence
steps.body: Once two triangles are congruent, every corresponding pair of sides and angles is equal. Match the vertices carefully: if $ABC \equiv PQR$ then $A \to P$, $B \to Q$, $C \to R$, so $AB = PQ$ and angle $C$ = angle $R$.

steps.text: $AB \to XY$, so $XY = 6$
$C \to Z$, so angle $Z = 52°$

check.prompt: Triangles $ABC$ and $PQR$ are congruent with $A \to P$, $B \to Q$, $C \to R$. Which side equals $BC$?

steps.title: Grade 9: writing a congruence proof
steps.body:
A proof has a fixed shape. State three equalities, each with a **reason** in brackets: given, midpoint, common side, opposite sides of a parallelogram, and so on. Name the condition. Then, if asked, use the congruence: corresponding angles are equal, and a further fact finishes the job.

$AB = AC$ (given). Angle $BAD$ = angle $CAD$ ($AD$ bisects angle $A$). $AD$ is common. So $ABD \equiv ACD$ (SAS). Hence $BD = DC$, so $AD$ bisects $BC$.

steps.text: 1. Three equalities, each with a reason
2. The condition: SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS
3. What follows: corresponding sides or angles are equal
4. The final fact that answers the question

check.prompt: In a congruence proof, which of these is a valid reason for two sides being equal?
check.solution: A reason must be a given fact or a known property. Using the conclusion is circular; the diagram is never a reason.
options: They look the same length in the diagram
$M$ is the midpoint of the side
The triangles are congruent (the thing being proved)

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- Congruent: same shape and size; rotation and reflection allowed.
- Conditions: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS. Not SSA, not AAA.
- The SAS angle must be between the two sides.
- Proof: three equalities with reasons, name the condition, then use it.

visuals.alt: Congruent triangles ABC and XYZ with one pair of corresponding sides and two pairs of corresponding angles marked equal (ASA)

questions.prompt: Two triangles are congruent. Which statement must be true?
questions.solution: Congruent means identical: every side and every angle matches, so shape and size are both the same.
options: They have the same shape and the same size
They have the same shape but may differ in size
They have the same area but may be different shapes

questions.prompt: Which is not a condition for two triangles to be congruent?
questions.solution: Three equal angles fix the shape but not the size: the triangles are similar, not necessarily congruent.

questions.prompt: The two triangles have three pairs of equal sides. Which condition shows they are congruent?

visual.alt: Two triangles with sides 7, 5 and 6 marked with one, two and three ticks, one rotated and flipped

questions.prompt: In the triangles shown, $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$ and angle $B$ = angle $E$. Which condition proves they are congruent?
questions.solution: The equal angle is between the two equal sides: side, angle, side.

visual.alt: Two triangles with two sides marked equal and the angle between them marked equal

questions.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has angle $A = 50°$, angle $B = 60°$ and $AB = 7$ cm. Triangle $XYZ$ has angle $X = 50°$, angle $Z = 70°$ and $XY = 7$ cm. Are the triangles congruent?
questions.skill: ASA with a third angle found
questions.solution: Angle $Y = 180 - 50 - 70 = 60°$. Then both triangles have $50°$, $60°$ and the 7 cm side between those angles: ASA.

questions.prompt: Two right-angled triangles have equal hypotenuses of 5 cm and one other pair of equal sides of 3 cm. Which condition shows congruence?
questions.solution: Right angle, hypotenuse, side: RHS. It works because Pythagoras fixes the third side.

visual.alt: Two right-angled triangles with hypotenuse 5 and a side 3, one rotated

questions.prompt: Triangles $ABC$ and $PQR$ are congruent with $AB = PQ$, $BC = QR$ and $AC = PR$. Angle $A = 48°$ and angle $B = 71°$. Work out angle $R$.

markScheme.description: Matches $R$ with $C$ or finds the third angle

questions.prompt: Triangle $LMN$ is congruent to triangle $XYZ$, with $L \to X$, $M \to Y$, $N \to Z$. $MN = 9$ cm. Which side of $XYZ$ is 9 cm?
questions.solution: $M \to Y$ and $N \to Z$, so $MN$ corresponds to $YZ$.

questions.prompt: $ABCD$ is a rectangle and $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Prove that triangles $AMD$ and $BMC$ are congruent.
questions.solution: Every line needs a reason in brackets. The examiner is marking the reasons, not the conclusion.

criteria.text: $AD = BC$ because opposite sides of a rectangle are equal
Angle $MAD$ = angle $MBC = 90°$ because a rectangle has right angles
Conclusion: congruent by SAS, with each fact given a reason

questions.modelAnswer: $AM = MB$ (M is the midpoint of $AB$). $AD = BC$ (opposite sides of a rectangle). Angle $DAM$ = angle $CBM = 90°$ (angles of a rectangle). Two sides and the included angle are equal, so triangles $AMD$ and $BMC$ are congruent by SAS.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, $AB = AC$ and $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Prove that angle $ADB = 90°$.
questions.skill: using congruence to prove a result
questions.solution: The structure is the whole answer: prove congruence, use it to equate two angles, use a second fact to pin them down.

criteria.text: Shows triangles $ABD$ and $ACD$ are congruent by SSS: $AB = AC$ (given), $BD = DC$ (midpoint), $AD$ common
Angle $ADB$ = angle $ADC$ because corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal
The two angles lie on a straight line so add to $180°$, hence each is $90°$

questions.modelAnswer: $AB = AC$ (given). $BD = DC$ ($D$ is the midpoint). $AD$ is common to both triangles. So triangles $ABD$ and $ACD$ are congruent by SSS. Therefore angle $ADB$ = angle $ADC$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles). Angles $ADB$ and $ADC$ lie on the straight line $BC$, so they add to $180°$, and each is $90°$.

questions.prompt: Two triangles each have sides of 7 cm and 5 cm and an angle of $40°$ that is not between those sides. Which statement is correct?
questions.solution: With the angle not between the sides, the arc from the end of the 7 cm side can cross in two places, giving two different triangles with the same three measurements. SSA is not a congruence condition.
options: They are not necessarily congruent, because SSA can give two different triangles
They are congruent by SAS, because two sides and an angle are equal in both triangles
They are congruent by SSA, because two sides and any angle are enough for congruence
They are congruent by ASA, because one angle and two sides are equal in both triangles

visual.alt: Two triangles sharing side 7, side 5 and a 40 degree angle not between them, with different third sides

questions.prompt: Triangle $PQR$ has $PQ = 8$ cm, $QR = 6$ cm and angle $PQR = 90°$. Triangle $XYZ$ has $XZ = 10$ cm, $YZ = 6$ cm and angle $XYZ = 90°$. The triangles are congruent. Work out the length of $XY$ in cm.
questions.solution: In $PQR$ the hypotenuse is $PR = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10$ cm. $XYZ$ has hypotenuse $XZ = 10$ and side $YZ = 6$, so it matches by RHS and $XY$ corresponds to $PQ = 8$ cm.

questions.prompt: $PQRS$ is a kite with $PQ = PS$ and $RQ = RS$. Prove that the diagonal $PR$ bisects angle $QPS$.
questions.solution: The common side is the fact students forget to write. Without it there is no third equality.

markScheme.description: Three equalities including the common side

criteria.text: Angle $QPR$ = angle $SPR$ (corresponding angles of congruent triangles), so $PR$ bisects angle $QPS$

questions.modelAnswer: $PQ = PS$ (given). $RQ = RS$ (given). $PR$ is common. So triangles $PQR$ and $PSR$ are congruent by SSS. Hence angle $QPR$ = angle $SPR$ (corresponding angles in congruent triangles), which means $PR$ bisects angle $QPS$.

questions.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has angles $30°$, $60°$, $90°$ and hypotenuse 10 cm. Triangle $DEF$ has angles $30°$, $60°$, $90°$ and its shortest side is 5 cm. Are the triangles congruent?
questions.skill: congruence from angles and one side
questions.solution: In a $30°$, $60°$, $90°$ triangle the shortest side is half the hypotenuse, so $DEF$ also has hypotenuse 10 cm. Equal angles with a matching side: congruent.
options: Yes: in a $30°$, $60°$, $90°$ triangle the shortest side is half the hypotenuse, so $DEF$ also has a 10 cm hypotenuse
No: the triangles have the same angles, so they are similar, but a 5 cm side and a 10 cm side mean they are different sizes
Yes: the three angles are equal, and matching angles (AAA) are always enough to prove that two triangles are congruent
It cannot be decided: congruence can only be checked when both triangles are drawn accurately on a diagram

questions.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. Prove that triangles $ABD$ and $CDB$ are congruent.
questions.solution: Two routes score: SSS with the common side, or ASA with alternate angles. Either way each line needs its reason.

markScheme.description: First pair of equal sides with reason

criteria.text: $AB = CD$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal)
$AD = CB$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal)

questions.modelAnswer: $AB = CD$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). $AD = CB$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). $BD$ is common to both triangles. So triangles $ABD$ and $CDB$ are congruent by SSS. An alternative uses alternate angles: angle $ABD$ = angle $CDB$ and angle $ADB$ = angle $CBD$ (alternate angles, $AB$ parallel to $DC$ and $AD$ parallel to $BC$) with $BD$ common, giving ASA.

questions.prompt: Two triangles have exactly the same three angles. One has sides twice as long as the other. Which statement is correct?
questions.solution: Same angles means the same shape: similar. Different sizes means not congruent. AAA is never a congruence condition for this reason.
options: They are similar but not congruent
They are neither similar nor congruent

questions.prompt: $ABCD$ is a rectangle with diagonal $AC$. Prove that triangles $ABC$ and $CDA$ are congruent.
questions.solution: A rectangle gives right angles and equal opposite sides; the diagonal is shared, so it is the hypotenuse of both triangles: RHS. A complete SSS proof, using $AB = CD$, $BC = DA$ and the common side $AC$, is equally correct.

markScheme.description: Angle ABC = angle CDA = 90° (angles of a rectangle)
AC is common to both triangles, and is the hypotenuse of each
AB = CD (opposite sides of a rectangle), so congruent by RHS

criteria.text: Angle $ABC$ = angle $CDA$ = $90°$, because $ABCD$ is a rectangle
$AC$ is a side of both triangles (common) and is the hypotenuse of each
$AB = CD$ as opposite sides of a rectangle, so the triangles are congruent by RHS (a complete SSS proof, adding $BC = DA$, scores full marks too)

questions.modelAnswer: Angle $ABC$ = angle $CDA$ = $90°$ because they are angles of a rectangle. $AC$ is common to both triangles and is the hypotenuse of each, since it is opposite the right angle. $AB = CD$ because opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. Right angle, hypotenuse and one side match, so triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $CDA$ by RHS.

examTechnique.body: Congruence questions come in two sizes: a 1 or 2 mark "which condition" question, and a 3 to 5 mark proof. In the proof every equality needs a reason in brackets, and the condition must be named. The marks are in the reasons: "it looks equal" is not one, and a proof is not finished until the shared side has been written down.
examinerErrors: Quoting SSA or AAA as a congruence condition.
Using SAS when the equal angle is not between the two equal sides.
Leaving out the reason for each equality in a proof.
Forgetting that a shared side is a valid third equality.
Matching the wrong vertices when reading off a corresponding side or angle.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer writes the proof in the standard shape without prompting, gives a reason for every line, chooses the condition that fits the given facts rather than the one that seems easiest, and then uses the congruence to reach the result asked for.
